Attleboro.not_found_notes: WORK-OFF: The city site gives $1,000 max / 73 hours / phone (Services page, undated) and age 60 / COA-administered / annual application with acceptance (FY26 Statutory Exemption Overview, 'UPDATED: 6/11/2025', https://www.cityofattleboro.us/DocumentCenter/View/13248/STATUTORY-EXEMPTION-OVERVIEW-FY26, quotes: 'SENIOR CITIZEN PROPERTY TAX WORK-OFF ABATEMENT – UP TO $1000.00 THIS PROGRAM IS ADMINISTED BY THE COUNCIL ON AGING' and '☐ You must be age 60.' and '☐ You must submit an application annually and be accepted into program through Council on Aging'). No income limit, signup window, hourly rate, or slot cap appears on any city page fetched. Hourly rate is NOT stated ($1,000 / 73 hrs would be about $13.70/hr, but that is my arithmetic, not a town figure). A search hit on uploads.weconnect.com (a third-party host, 'Revised 09.2021' application) shows different terms (47 hours for $600; runs Jan 1 to Nov 15). It is NOT a town domain, so I did not use it. It is also older than and conflicts with the $1,000/73-hour city page. attleboroseniorcenter.com returned a 'Temporarily Unavailable' page and is not on the city domain; not used. Address source: COA page https://www.cityofattleboro.us/351/Council-On-Aging-Department ('Attleboro Senior Center 25 S Main Street Attleboro MA 02703'). 41C: No FY2027 41C figures are posted; the newest city figures are FY2026 (overview updated 6/11/2025), and FY2027 limits may differ. The FY26 41C brochure (https://www.cityofattleboro.us/DocumentCenter/View/13254/FY26-Senior-Exemption-Clause-41C-Brochure) shows identical income/asset figures and the deadline ('We require the form to be into the Assessor’s Office no later than April 1st.'), but its footer reads 'Updated:5/23/23'. The two city sources agree; no conflict. It says $300 comes off each of the 3rd and 4th quarter bills. No §5C½ additional exemption is mentioned. Assessor ext. 3133 comes from the 41C brochure ('508-223-2222 Ext. 3133'); x3131 comes from https://www.cityofattleboro.us/151/Assessors-Office ('For General Questions 508-223-2222 x-3131'). The site's /Search endpoint renders results client-side and returned nothing usable. The Recycling-Rubbish page (/221) and its Solid Waste Abatement form mention no senior discount. I found no CPA senior exemption on the city site.

The application also says 'Placement in this program is based on availability of suitable work.' Hourly rate is NOT stated ($1,500 / 100 hrs implies $15/hr, but that is my arithmetic, not a town figure). CONFLICTING STALE TOWN SOURCES are still online. (a) 2018 news item https://www.arlingtonma.gov/Home/Components/News/News/7317 ('Post Date:01/24/2018'; 'Seniors have the opportunity to volunteer 136 hours to get a $1,500 property tax relief benefit.'). (b) FY2020 COA flyer https://www.arlingtonma.gov/home/showdocument?id=47699 (125 hours; income up to $58,000 single / $88,000 joint / $73,000 HoH). Both are stale=true and superseded by the FY27 application (100 hours; $75k/$112k/$94k); do not show them. 41C: The FY2027 Property Tax Relief Programs booklet (66617) agrees: '$1,300' and 'The filing deadline for FY 2027 is April 1, 2027'. Its footnote says the income figures include the Social Security/government-pension deduction. No §5C½ additional amount is mentioned; I cannot tell whether $1,300 includes a local increase. MINOR WORDING CONFLICT on the E&D Tax Relief Fund: the booklet says 'Low-income Seniors with a state recognized disability', while the FY2027 application says 60+ OR state-recognized disability. The application is the more specific, newer document. Water/sewer: I checked the Water & Sewer page and rate schedule and found no senior discount.
